translationRepairs: Under Prince Rui's regency Tan Tai enjoyed the confidence of Tulai, chief of the bayara guard, and Sonin of the Council of Deliberation alike.
Under Prince Rui's regency Tan Tai, together with Tulai, chief of the bayara guard, and Sonin the investigatory secretary, all enjoyed the prince's trust.

s0027 has 譚泰與…圖賴、…索尼並見信任: the three men alike received Prince Rui's trust. The before line reverses the trust relation (Tan Tai enjoying theirs) and mis-titles 啟心郎 as Council of Deliberation; the proposed wording restores both.
He was soon told to garrison Xi'an; marching through Henan he put down bandits in Dingxi and Pingliang, including Liu Hongqi.
He was soon told to garrison Xi'an; marching through Henan he put down the Xiping bandits, including Liu Hongqi.
s0082 has 討定西平土寇: 討定 is the verb 'suppress/pacify' and 西平 is the place Xiping (on the Henan route to Xi'an), not Dingxi and Pingliang. The proposed idiomatic replacement corrects that toponym error.
He was soon ordered to lead troops to garrison Xi'an; passing through Henan he suppressed the bandits of Dingxi and Pingliang such as Liu Hongqi.
He was soon ordered to lead troops to garrison Xi'an; passing through Henan he suppressed the bandits of Xiping such as Liu Hongqi.
Same reading as the idiomatic line: 西平 is one place name after 討定, not Dingxi plus Pingliang. The proposed literal correctly renders 西平土寇 as the bandits of Xiping.
When Prince Su returned, Beile Tunqi and others impeached him; He Luohui testified again, and the prince lost his title and died under house arrest.
When Prince Su returned, Beizi Tunqi and others impeached him; He Luohui testified again, and the prince lost his title and died under house arrest.
s0092 has 貝子屯齊: 貝子 is Beizi, distinct from 貝勒 (Beile). The proposed change corrects only that title.
After Prince Rui's death, when the Shizu took power, He Luohui told Beile Xi Han: "The Yellow Banner ministers hate me; I denounced Prince Su—will they spare me now?"
After Prince Rui's death, when the Shizu took power, He Luohui told Beizi Xi Han: "The Yellow Banner ministers hate me; I denounced Prince Su—will they spare me now?"
s0095 has 貝子錫翰: again 貝子, not 貝勒. Replacing Beile with Beizi matches the Chinese title.

In the seventh year, when Prince Rui fell ill and resented the emperor's absence, Leng Sengji and Xi Han asked the throne to visit; though Prince Rui punished the request, an amnesty restored him and Leng Sengji was made a first-class baron.

In the seventh year, when Prince Rui fell ill and resented the emperor's absence, Leng Sengji and Beizi Xi Han asked the throne to visit; Leng Sengji was reduced in hereditary rank for the unauthorized request, then an amnesty restored him and advanced him to first-class baron.

After 冷僧機及貝子錫翰等奏請上臨視, 睿親王坐以擅請降世職 names Prince Rui as the punisher who reduced hereditary rank for unauthorized solicitation; 恩詔復故，進一等伯 then restores and advances Leng Sengji. The before line muddles who was demoted; the proposed wording correctly assigns the demotion–amnesty–advancement to Leng Sengji and restores Beizi for Xi Han.
Xitu Ku and Boerhui too had long service with merit.
Xitu Ku and Boerhui too had long followed campaigns with merit.

s0193 has 久從征戰有勞: 征戰 specifies campaign/warfare service. Omitting it as mere 'long service' drops that military content; the proposed 'long followed campaigns with merit' restores it without over-rewriting.
Boerhui and others exposed Xitu Ku: each denouncing the other, they all went to execution together.
Xitu Ku's execution was exposed by Boerhui and others: each denouncing the other, they all went to execution together.
s0195 opens with 錫圖庫之誅，博爾輝等發之: the topic is Xitu Ku's execution, which Boerhui and others exposed. The before line flattens that to 'exposed Xitu Ku'; the proposed wording restores the 之誅 framing.
